concepts.definition: The frames-and-context family F1 concerns finite actors declaring, sizing, binding, activating, relating, auditing and revising bounded reference frames. REFERENCE_FRAME owns engagement law in urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation; ACTIVATION owns context construction and FOUNDATIONS owns the referenced frame objects, authority kinds, independence distinctions and frame tuple. The foundation-to-law table traces rules and choices without owning those rules.

grounding.quote:
This family, frames and context (F1 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law)),
decides how a finite actor engages a body of work through bounded reference
frames: how a frame is declared, sized, bound, activated, related to other
frames, used to audit coverage and revised.

concepts.label: Frames and context

concepts.definition: A reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required by one evaluation family. It is a relation specification, not a required schema or runtime carrier. Its engagement atomicity means activation and evaluation as one bounded attention unit; it does not imply semantic irreducibility.

grounding.quote: a reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations one evaluation family requires.

A reference frame is atomic at engagement altitude: it is activated and
evaluated as one bounded attention unit. Semantic irreducibility is a
separate question: one frame may contain several semantic atoms, and one
semantic atom may take part in several frames

concepts.label: Reference frame

concepts.definition: The questions or predicates a frame declares it supports at its declared coordinates, together with its closed result algebra. This declaration supplies the boundary against which sufficiency can be tested.

grounding.quote:
Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary

concepts.label: Evaluation family

concepts.definition: A selected actor's declared limits and capabilities, including competence, context capacity, access and tools. An activated attention surface must fit this envelope; adequate attention in actual use is a separate evidential question.

grounding.quote:
Whether the actor attends adequately to a frame that fits is a separate
question, answered by actual-use evidence under
[EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification); a size measurement
does not answer it

concepts.label: Capability envelope

concepts.definition: Authority admitted from its existing owner and scope. Frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authority remain distinguishable, with actor identity apart; frame-set authority is human authority. An authority proxy remains distinct from the human authority.

grounding.quote: the division into frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authority, with actor identity apart, and frame-set authority as human authority: FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds

concepts.label: Admitted authority

concepts.definition: A semantic atom is a domain meaning unit whose irreducibility is distinct from engagement atomicity. A domain's semantic-contraction law, where supplied by an adopting method, governs that domain atom family.

grounding.quote:
Where an adopting
method supplies a semantic-contraction law for its domain atoms, that law
governs the domain atom family.

concepts.label: Semantic atom

concepts.definition: Human-declared project method structure comprising selected frames, evaluation inventory, capability envelopes, overlaps, checks, dependencies, authorities, exclusions, residual uncertainty and revision conditions for a governed workspace and outcome. It need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may declare an initial project frame set from accumulated
development practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the governed
outcome's risk and knowledge of the available agents and other actors.
a frame set need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology

concepts.label: Frame set

conditions: An evaluation was performed.
concepts.definition: One closed result in the declared core algebra or a lawful refinement mapped into it. The five named core values are satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis; FOUNDATIONS §4 owns their meanings. A nonperformed evaluation has no evaluation result.

grounding.quote:
Every performed evaluation of a frame returns one closed result in the
frame's declared result algebra: the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), or a refinement mapped
into it under that section. That section owns the five core values
(`satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame` and
`invalid_basis`)

concepts.label: Closed evaluation result

concepts.definition: Seven relations distinct from the frame: declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities) → frame_set; activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor) → activated_frame or activation_refusal; evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence) → result plus evidence plus residuals; conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results) → decision, conflict or indeterminate; translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping) → translated_value, declared_loss or refusal; audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set) → coverage_ledger; revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) → proposed_frame_set_delta. These signatures describe relations rather than callable software interfaces; subsequent text supplements the signatures' outcome lists.

grounding.quote:
declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities)
  -> frame_set

activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor)
  -> activated_frame | activation_refusal

evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence)
  -> result + evidence + residuals

conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results)
  -> decision | conflict | indeterminate

translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping)
  -> translated_value | declared_loss | refusal

audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set)
  -> coverage_ledger

revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change)
  -> proposed_frame_set_delta

concepts.label: Method functions

concepts.definition: A declared decision rule consumes closed results of several frames using the conjunction and core values owned by FOUNDATIONS §4. REFERENCE_FRAME defines the frame relation and outcome refinement, not another conjunction.

grounding.quote:
A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.
The rule, what it must state, and the conjunction it computes are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
over the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results);
this member defines no conjunction of its own.

concepts.label: Result conjunction

concepts.definition: One frame supplies a value or evidence consumed inside another through a declared translation. Its fields are source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.

grounding.quote:
One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another. The
translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions

concepts.label: Evidence or coordinate translation

conditions: The evaluation requires composition.
concepts.definition: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation, declared by the owning application.

grounding.quote:
Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
relation. The owning application declares the composition

concepts.label: Material composition

concepts.definition: Named frame relation categories: disjoint shares no material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for the declared evaluations; overlapping shares some material variables, evidence or entities; complementary evaluations jointly inform one decision; alternative frames evaluate the same claim under declared capability or evidence conditions; refinement resolves another frame's aggregated material distinction; restriction evaluates a lawful subset of another's domain; translated moves values or evidence through a declared coordinate map; temporally successive evaluates a changed basis later; composed combines frame relations into one governed evaluation or action; governing/subordinate inherits declared constraints where real authority or decomposition exists.

grounding.quote:
- governing and subordinate: one frame inherits declared constraints from
  another where a real authority or decomposition relation exists.

concepts.label: Frame relation categories

concepts.definition: Exchange of information between frames or their activated actors. Communication is distinct from functional decomposition, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject topology and evaluation dependency.

grounding.quote:
Communication is the exchange of
information between frames, or between the actors activated on them. An
exchange by itself grants no authority

concepts.label: Communication

concepts.definition: Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T) binds workspace, governed outcome, exact basis, known evaluation inventory, declared frame set, and claim time or immutable checkpoint.

grounding.quote:
Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the
workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known
evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable
checkpoint T of the claim.

concepts.label: Coverage basis

concepts.definition: The known material evaluations derived by the coverage evaluator from every material available source, with provenance and materiality recorded.

grounding.quote:
The coverage evaluator derives the known evaluation inventory from every
material available source

concepts.label: Evaluation inventory

concepts.definition: Cross-cutting audit lenses, typically outcome/capability, identity/authority, lifecycle/temporal behaviour, topology/interaction seams, transport/representation, evidence/proof, change/failure/recovery/rollback, historical regression, and actor capability/context fit. A lens becomes a frame only when separately instantiated as a bounded evaluation family.

grounding.quote:
These are lenses (FOUNDATIONS §2): they become frames only when separately
instantiated as bounded evaluation families

concepts.label: Coverage dimensions

concepts.definition: Per-evaluation audit record whose status answers whether, on the declared coverage tuple, a capable selected frame covers the evaluation without unresolved frame/result/authority conflict, or a cited governing authority excludes it. Baseline statuses are covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown and excluded_by_authority.

grounding.quote:
They answer
whether a row's coverage obligation is met, for the predicate "on the
declared coverage tuple, a capable frame of S covers the evaluation with
no unresolved conflict among the frames, results or authorities that
cover it, or a governing authority the row cites excludes it".

concepts.label: Coverage ledger

concepts.definition: Ordered examination of activation, exact subject/basis, actor capability, admissible evidence, missing material variables/invariants, missing conjunction/translation, evaluation-family adequacy and only then the need for another frame.

grounding.quote:
1. Was the correct declared frame activated?
2. Were the subject and basis exact?
3. Was the actor inside the capability envelope?
4. Was admissible evidence available?
5. Is a material variable or invariant missing from the frame?
6. Is a required conjunction or translation missing?
7. Is the evaluation family itself wrong or incomplete?
8. Is another frame required?

concepts.label: Frame diagnosis

concepts.definition: Carrier-neutral packet for one activated frame or declared active frame configuration. The minimal binding template identifies the activation and resolves the frame, exact evaluation, subject, basis, attention, actor, authorities, evidence, inter-frame relations, result return and stop/change conditions.

grounding.quote:
An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
workspace from ambient context

The following carrier-neutral content is sufficient to bind one declared
frame for one evaluation.

concepts.label: Activation packet and binding template

concepts.definition: Three carrier-neutral document shapes supplying the least content to declare a frame, frame set and evaluation result. They are source templates, not populated declarations or executed evaluations.

grounding.quote:
The three carrier-neutral shapes below are the least content that declares
a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result. Each is sufficient as
written in Markdown or any other consumer-selected carrier

concepts.label: Minimal declaration templates

concepts.definition: A historical mapping from received rc.2 REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD anchors to dispositions and successor loci; unqualified loci refer to REFERENCE_FRAME. Rows received by FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION or EVALUATION are listed there. This section records dispositions rather than deciding substantive law.

grounding.quote:
RF rows received by this member. Rows that land in FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION
or EVALUATION are listed in those members. Anchors are into rc.2
REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless it names
another member.

concepts.label: Source disposition register

concepts.definition: Tier-2 RELEASE owns release publication: bounded context, release identities, project-qualified references/subtrees, historical reference conservation, candidate construction, immutable RC publication, exact-cut qualification, monotonic version-line advancement, selectors, naming, scoped assets, Product subject, release-matched asset cohorts, acceptance, external qualification dependencies and successor baseline conservation STDO-UP-015 with its dispositions. Its context identity is urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication under the selected complete STDO basis. It owns qualification/publication/selection transitions, not Product meaning or consumer adoption.

grounding.quote:
Tier 2. Owns release publication: the release-publication bounded
context, release identities, project-qualified refs and the project
subtree, historical ref conservation, the three phases with candidate
construction, immutable RC publication, exact-cut qualification and
monotonic version-line advancement

This member owns the release-publication bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication` under the selected complete
STDO basis. It owns the identities and transitions used to qualify,
publish and select released cuts. It does not own Product meaning or
consumer adoption

concepts.label: Release publication

concepts.definition: A published immutable point-in-time RC cut with product-local name v<version>-rc.<n>. Release process evaluates, bounds, names, publishes and makes the cut discoverable, distinct from live specification's current constitutional project truth.

grounding.quote:
Release process is distinct from live project specification. Live
specification defines the current constitutional truth of the project.
Release process defines how one published point-in-time cut is evaluated,
bounded, named, published and made discoverable

concepts.label: Release cut

concepts.definition: The mutable product-local v<version> selector points to the latest published immutable RC for its project and version line, where latest is the greatest published positive RC ordinal. It is a discovery aid.

grounding.quote:
It denotes a mutable version-line selector (FOUNDATIONS §2). The selector
points to the latest published immutable RC cut on that line, where latest
means the greatest positive RC ordinal published for that project and
version line.

concepts.label: Version-line selector

conditions: The family governs work with the stated instance premises.

grounding.quote:
They are conditions of the work this family governs, not
commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone.

constraints.statement: Instance premises are: workspace material exceeds one actor's competence/context/tools/access envelope; evaluations are declared questions about a governed outcome; multiple frames and actors may overlap; workspace/topology/capabilities change between activations; actors may read owners and copied/projected/compressed surfaces. These are work conditions, not commitments derived from finitude. P0's named actor-change premise permits a different next actor to reacquire declared sources, not private memory; its open-world premise says the world is open. Engagement law supplies no application profile, role mapping, product-owned frame-basis binding, domain product, runtime, workflow or assurance implementation. Specialisations retain their own owners and neither enter nor amend this member by proximity or matching names. Imported concepts retain owner and meaning through reference-only import, granting no semantic/evaluation/operation/decision authority; refinements name their owner and map to the core.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete P0–P6 statements and their standing are external to the supplied sections.

grounding.quote: A frame is bound only when every material coordinate resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition, and representation cannot create, widen or replace that binding

constraints.statement: Every material coordinate must resolve to exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition before a frame is bound. Prompt, context packet and program are projections of an activated frame; representations cannot create, widen or replace its binding. FOUNDATIONS owns the twelve-component tuple ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩.
constraints.uncertainty: The twelve component definitions are not supplied.

grounding.quote: The context starts as the material closure of the intake's seed set (the subject, outcome and affected relations it names) under that relation family, and a closure that is not finite and unique on the exact basis stops the step and is not guessed

constraints.statement: Context construction starts from material closure of the intake's named subject, outcome and affected relations under the material relation family. If closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis, stop without guessing, with closure_unresolved as owned by ACTIVATION. Project closure to selected context and record its boundary, including excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. The table refers closure law to AC-010 and projection to AC-011.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced closure and projection calculus is not supplied.

conditions: Acquiring declared inputs or activating a reusable frame.

grounding.quote: a declared input absent from the actor's view is neither licence to read elsewhere nor evidence that it is absent, and a candidate source, a moving selector or another basis is no substitute.

constraints.statement: Acquire inputs by exact identity only from the exact selected basis. Absence from view gives neither permission to read elsewhere nor evidence of absence; candidate source, moving selector and another basis cannot substitute. A stale, missing or question-insufficient derived surface requires direct acquisition of deciding owner sections. Acquisition is read-only and grants no role, operation or decision; return a missing binding with its outcome before dependent action. Activation binds exact subject/basis and loads declared material relations/evidence, never an undifferentiated workspace dump. A reusable declaration proves no particular activation correct. If no available frame/actor pair can lawfully evaluate, return out_of_frame or the refusal whose cause holds without implied-context continuation. Configuration allocates frame selection to actor or assigning authority.
constraints.uncertainty: Full acquisition, configuration and stop-state rules belong to unsupplied ACTIVATION sections.

conditions: A derived surface, projected frame or prompt is used.

grounding.quote: For a question another member owns, or one that joins the law of several owners, the step returns `out_of_frame` naming the owning members, and the question is decided from those members or from a derived surface whose declared sources include every owner
Construction starts from the highest live authority surface the question needs and names an unresolved upstream authority gap before fallback context is read

constraints.statement: A derived surface owns no determination and decides standalone only questions its declared source members own. For another owner's question or joined-owner law, return out_of_frame naming owners and decide from those owners or a surface declaring every owner. A prompt is a rendered contract over typed authority, not source law; it projects currently needed authority references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations, fallback conditions and selected acquisition material. Historical workaround prose is carried only where a current surface still needs the constraint. Construction begins at the highest live authority surface needed and identifies an upstream authority gap before fallback reading.
constraints.uncertainty: The named design, ODD, UX and ticket specialisations are external references.

grounding.quote:
Unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful pressure for
   reconfiguration; they are neither failed evaluations nor implied
   acceptance

constraints.statement: The ten claims state: no finite actor is presumed to attend to the whole material workspace; a useful frame is finite and sufficient for its declared evaluation family; evaluation determines attention; human authority may declare practical sets from practice without mechanical unique partition; overlap/composition/refinement/restriction/translation/succession are permitted and hierarchy optional; joint frame use does not require composing internal coordinates; coverage is workspace/outcome/inventory/basis/time-relative; breadth/usefulness/actor/technology gives selection or result no semantic/operation/decision authority; unknown and out-of-frame results are reconfiguration pressure, neither failed evaluations nor acceptance; historical failures/resets/invisible violations are improvement evidence. These claims add no rules beyond their cited laws.

conditions: A frame is declared or activated.

grounding.quote:
Every frame, declared or activated, obeys the following. The objects named
are defined in FOUNDATIONS §2.

constraints.statement: The following frame laws apply to every declared and activated frame; their named objects are owned by FOUNDATIONS §2.

grounding.quote:
Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary

constraints.statement: Every frame declares its supported evaluation family; sufficiency is testable only against that family. Modules, files, services, roles, personas, prompts or lenses without a declared evaluation relation do not qualify as frames. Family membership requires that the decided question be stated by the family at the declared coordinates; names, similar wording and frame-set membership cannot establish it.

conditions: The frame is activated.
Size measurement applies where the actor envelope declares context capacity.

grounding.quote:
An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the
selected actor's declared capability envelope. A frame that needs
undeclared ambient memory, conversation history or an effectively global
workspace context is not reconstructable for that actor

Where the envelope declares a context capacity, the selected context's size is measured before the actor reads it, over a stated boundary, and recorded with the capacity and the comparison; context outside the boundary is recorded as not measured.

constraints.statement: Activated attention must be finite, fit the selected declared envelope and be reconstructable without undeclared memory/history/global workspace context. Where capacity is declared, measure selected context before reading over a stated boundary and record size, capacity and comparison; mark outside context unmeasured. Envelope owns capacity and byte/token unit; execution binding owns boundary and time/spend/other limits. The measurement applies only at that boundary, proves fit only, and is neither budget nor universal gate. ACTIVATION §2 owns measurement applicability; actual-use evidence under EVALUATION §7 decides adequate attention separately.

conditions: A known relation's lawful change can alter result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency, operation authority or decision authority.
exceptions: No proof that all undiscovered material relations are absent is required.

grounding.quote:
Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result,
the validity of the basis, the sufficiency of evidence, operation authority
or decision authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared
authoritative input. Omitting a material relation makes the frame
insufficient.

constraints.statement: Every such known material relation must appear in the frame or enter through a declared authoritative input. Omission makes the frame insufficient; relations not held are not thereby absent.

conditions: A relation cannot affect the declared evaluation.
exceptions: The relation is needed to establish that irrelevance.

grounding.quote:
Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation stay outside active
attention unless they are needed to establish that irrelevance. A frame
does not expand because adjacent workspace material exists

constraints.statement: Keep irrelevant relations outside active attention except where establishing irrelevance requires them. Adjacent material or corpus availability alone does not justify loading, reading or frame expansion.

grounding.quote:
Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence
scope. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns
`invalid_basis` or requires reactivation. Apparent equality never
substitutes for declared coordinate equality

constraints.statement: Every result binds exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence scope. Stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis yields invalid_basis or requires reactivation. Names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology positions cannot substitute for coordinate equality under the frame's declared coordinate/equality law.

exceptions: Authority kinds may coincide in a lawful case, without default collapse.

grounding.quote:
A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen,
transfer or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation or decision
authority from anything that creates none.

A read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; an effectful one inherits the exact operation grant from its existing owner. A proxy for human authority keeps its identity distinct from the human authority's

constraints.statement: Frames carry/apply admitted authority but cannot mint, widen, transfer or reconstruct it from actor identity, capability, evidence shape, implementation reachability, selection, declaration, activation, execution or role names. Read-only evaluations declare no operation authority; effectful evaluations inherit the existing owner's exact operation grant. Actor identity is not authority; proxies retain identities distinct from human authority.

exceptions: One actor may lawfully perform several roles, while their distinctions remain.

grounding.quote:
a frame declaration keeps these roles distinguishable even when
one actor lawfully performs several of them, and where the evaluation
performs a material operation, the existing operation owner supplies the
exact grant as a further role the declaration keeps apart
The evaluator applies the frame's declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra and records every assumption whose failure could change the result

constraints.statement: Keep semantic law, evidence observations, evaluator application, existing operation-owner grant and disposing decision authority distinguishable. Apply declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra, recording every assumption whose failure could change the result. EVALUATION §2 owns the separation; RF-007 binds it to frames.

conditions: Frames share material or an evaluation uses a cross-frame equality/translation.

grounding.quote:
Frames may share entities, variables, evidence or coordinates. Shared
material establishes neither identical meaning nor identical basis,
authority or result. Every cross-frame equality or translation an
evaluation uses is declared where it is used

constraints.statement: Sharing entities, variables, evidence or coordinates establishes no identity of meaning, basis, authority or result. Declare every used cross-frame equality or translation at its use.

exceptions: A consumer may explicitly align structures where the governed subject warrants it.

grounding.quote:
Parent
and child relations apply only where explicitly declared. Functional
decomposition, communication, authority precedence, frame configuration,
subject topology and evaluation dependency are distinct relation
structures

No relation is the default universal frame topology. A project declares
only the relations its evaluations and coverage claims need

constraints.statement: Parent/child relations apply only if explicitly declared. Keep functional decomposition, communication, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject topology and evaluation dependency distinct; do not silently collapse them into a hierarchy. Communication alone grants no authority and establishes neither decomposition nor evaluation dependency. Configuration may assign exchanges and responsibilities without converting an exchange to a grant or dependency. No relation is a default topology; declare only relations needed for evaluations and coverage.

conditions: Composition law is required when the evaluation combines internal variables, transports values/evidence across frames or treats operations as one material execution relation.
exceptions: Separate activations may instead deliver closed results to a declared conjunction or decision rule.

grounding.quote:
Using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds.
Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines
their internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or
treats their operations as one material execution relation.

constraints.statement: Using several frames alone imposes no internal-manifold composition requirement. Require composition law only for the stated material combinations, and introduce material composition only where evaluation requires it.

conditions: A frame is activated; a material topology mutation or material frame revision is detected.

grounding.quote:
An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating
its coordinates or its materiality judgment. A detected material topology
mutation causes reevaluation, frame revision or recharting before the
previous result is reused.

constraints.statement: Declare topology changes capable of invalidating coordinates or materiality judgments. A detected material mutation requires reevaluation, revision or recharting before reuse. Material frame revision invalidates for reuse every result bound to the prior revision, subject to the recorded recheck routes in Revision actions.

grounding.quote:
nothing is
coerced to success; that a refinement adds no core value, keeps
indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit and raises
no result's standing; and that an evaluation not performed has no result

constraints.statement: Each performed evaluation returns exactly one closed result under its declared core algebra or mapped refinement. Nothing is coerced to success. Refinement adds no core value, elevates no standing and preserves indeterminate/out_of_frame/invalid_basis pressure explicitly. Nonperformance yields no evaluation result; its stop state belongs to ACTIVATION §3. RF-012 applies, but does not define, these core rules.
constraints.uncertainty: The full core meanings and stop-state algebra are external.

conditions: A fresh competent actor is inside the declared envelope.

grounding.quote:
A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can
reconstruct the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, the exact
subject, the basis and the admissible inputs, without undocumented
conversational or historical context

constraints.statement: The activated evaluation must be reconstructable from declaration, exact subject, basis and admissible inputs without undocumented conversational or historical context.

conditions: The material manifold exceeds the selected actor's envelope.

grounding.quote:
Choosing among them is human authority's, exercised directly or
in advance through the grant; ACTIVATION §2 says which of them a step
selects itself and which re-enter the grant's owner. The actor may not
silently omit material relations to fit its context
the lawful responses are another actor, a refined frame or outer contract, sequenced activations, a lawful compression or `out_of_frame`

constraints.statement: Adequacy includes actor usability. Lawful responses include another actor, refined frame or outer contract, sequencing, lawful compression or out_of_frame. Human authority chooses directly or through advance grant: refinement/sequencing/compression may be selected within grant, while another actor or larger envelope re-enters its owner under ACTIVATION §2. Never silently omit material relations or exceed the envelope. Greater capability may change size/sequence but waives no invariant and widens no authority.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION §2 owns the complete remedy and allocation rules.

grounding.quote:
Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved
relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability
stay explicit. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of
universal completeness

constraints.statement: Keep unresolved relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability explicit in evaluation and coverage results. No recorded counterexample does not establish universal completeness.

grounding.quote:
This member requires the declared relations and the observable outcomes.
It requires no frame runtime, universal carrier, registry, controller,
prompt format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count or
software framework

constraints.statement: Require declared relations and observable outcomes, without requiring runtime, universal carrier, registry, controller, prompt format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count or software framework.

conditions: Compressing practice or merging frames.

grounding.quote:
A frame compresses accumulated practice when its declaration preserves the
material distinctions and failure detections its evaluation family requires
while fitting its capability envelope.
Whether a compression preserved what the evaluation needs is a claim: the compressing step records the compression and its preservation argument

constraints.statement: Preserve required material distinctions and failure detections while fitting the envelope; no unique smallest frame is required. Retain intentional overlap supporting independent activation, different capability fit, evidence altitude or useful fault detection. Merge only if evaluation meaning, authority, capability fit and proportional reasoning cost survive. Record compression and preservation argument as a claim; the promotion served determines whether independent assessment is required.

conditions: Considering frame-set contraction.

grounding.quote:
Frame-set contraction asks a different
question: whether two frame declarations support the same evaluation
relation without material difference in evidence, authority, capability
fit, evaluation or assurance independence, or failure detection.

constraints.statement: Frame contraction asks whether declarations support the same evaluation relation without material difference in evidence, authority, capability fit, evaluation independence, assurance independence or failure detection. Overlapping material variables alone do not justify contraction to a disjoint minimum; a domain semantic-contraction law does not become a frame-set contraction law.

conditions: Human authority declares a project frame set.
constraints.statement: Record governed workspace/outcome, known evaluation inventory, selected frames/envelopes, intentional overlaps/separate checks, known dependencies/translations, semantic/evaluation/decision/acceptance authority and operation authority where material, known exclusions/residual uncertainty and revision conditions. Human selection is lawful method structure but proves neither completeness nor frame authority over inspected relations.

conditions: Selecting a set S for known material evaluations E(W,G).

grounding.quote:
for every
evaluation e in E(W, G), there is a frame F in S and an available actor a
inside F's capability envelope K_F such that F with a is capable of e

Frame selection
cannot waive another applicable semantic, authority, evidence or
independence constraint

constraints.statement: Baseline coverage holds when every e in E(W,G) has some F in S and an available actor inside K_F such that F with that actor can evaluate e. Also weigh actor context/competence, risk/consequence, acquisition/reasoning cost, evidence availability, useful independent overlap, translation/reconciliation cost, historical blind spots and reversibility of inadequacy. No optimisation algorithm is prescribed. These considerations impose no universal ledger, benchmark, budget or measurement gate. Resource control applies only through an explicitly selected frame and its owning applicability/work scope; ACTIVATION §6 is selected where cost is the governed claim. RF-002 fit measurement remains distinct. Selection waives no applicable semantic, authority, evidence or independence constraint.

conditions: Interpreting activate outcomes for its activation predicate.

grounding.quote: | | `activation_refusal(basis)` | the subject or basis is stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched (RF-005), a topology mismatch included: the subject's topology is not the topology basis the frame declares (RF-011) | `invalid_basis` |

constraints.statement: Each outcome carries its function predicate and exactly one core value. For activate: activated_frame → satisfied iff declaration is bound to exact evaluation/subject/basis/actor; activation_refusal(capability) → out_of_frame when a declared required capability is absent from actor envelope, naming capability and owner where given; activation_refusal(authority) → out_of_frame when needed semantic/evaluation/operation/decision authority is unadmitted, naming owner; activation_refusal(basis) → invalid_basis for stale/advanced/ambiguous/mismatched subject or basis, including topology mismatch. If no usable frame declares a required material relation or capability, activate returns out_of_frame directly. Activation outcomes answer activation, never the evaluation claim; refused activation performs no evaluation.

conditions: Interpreting conjoin under its declared decision rule.

grounding.quote: | | `conflict` | the conjunction reports `falsified` while mandatory results for the same claim disagree, one `satisfied` and another `falsified`; the counterexample survives the join, and the disagreement stays unresolved for the decision authority | `falsified` |

A planned
assessment without a closed result, and required coverage that no planned
assessment addresses, are no outcome of `conjoin`:

constraints.statement: For the composite predicate: decision(holds) → satisfied when conjunction reports satisfied; decision(fails) → falsified when conjunction reports falsified and no mandatory result for that claim is satisfied; conflict → falsified when mandatory same-claim results include both satisfied and falsified, retaining the counterexample and unresolved disagreement for decision authority; indeterminate → indeterminate. Conjoin returns out_of_frame or invalid_basis directly when conjunction reports it, including basis mismatch, despite omission from the signature. Declared veto/deferral follows the reported value's applicable cause or direct return. Planned assessments without closed results and required coverage without a planned assessment are recorded beside the value, are not conjoin outcomes and map to no core value. decision(holds) is assessment, not acceptance; acceptance is separate.
constraints.uncertainty: The governing conjunction computation, veto and deferral law are externally owned.

conditions: Interpreting translate for whether value/evidence enters the target as declared.

grounding.quote: | | `declared_loss` | the value or evidence is carried with a loss inside the declared accepted loss; the loss travels with it as a residual (P4b) | `satisfied` |

constraints.statement: translated_value → satisfied when carried into target coordinates with declared meaning; declared_loss → satisfied when loss is within accepted loss and travels as residual; refusal(condition) → falsified when a declared refusal holds, loss exceeds accepted loss, or identity/equality fails under declared equality law; refusal(authority) → out_of_frame for an authority mismatch whose relation to target semantic/evaluation/operation/decision authority is declared neither preserved nor a refusal condition, naming owner; refusal(basis) → invalid_basis for stale/advanced/ambiguous/mismatched source basis or coordinate. Outcomes keep predicate, cause, core value and locally owned meaning together; refusal or excess loss cannot be mistaken for success.

grounding.quote: | `conditionally_covered` | a capable frame of S covers it only under a condition the audit has not established; the residual names the condition and the evidence that would decide it | `indeterminate` |

an evaluation whose row is `uncovered` is required
coverage that no planned assessment addresses
([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)), never a

constraints.statement: Each audit status carries its predicate and exactly one core value: covered → satisfied for a capable selected frame evaluating on the tuple without unresolved covering conflict; separately_covered → satisfied for separate selected-frame activations each evaluating without unresolved conflict; excluded_by_authority → satisfied for cited governing exclusion; conditionally_covered → indeterminate where an unestablished condition limits coverage, with condition and deciding evidence in residual; conflicted → falsified for unresolved covering frame/result/authority conflict, retained for decision authority; uncovered → falsified where no capable selected frame evaluates and no cited exclusion applies; unknown → indeterminate where admissible evidence cannot decide coverage, including unknown capability/materiality. These are audit results, never results of the evaluated claim. Exclusion meets the obligation without establishing coverage or performance and is not failure. An uncovered row is an unaddressed coverage obligation in conjunction over the governed claim, not a falsified component. Conditional/conflicted/unknown/uncovered must not be read as covered.
